```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(svyexpo)
```

This vignette shows how to give each person an exposure over time windows you
choose, using simulated data. You need a table of people with an identifier, a
date and coordinates, and an exposure in any of four forms.

```{r people}
people <- data.frame(
  id   = 1:4,
  date = as.Date(c("2019-03-10", "2019-07-22", "2019-11-05", "2020-02-14")),  # birth dates
  lon  = c(-0.200, -0.198, -0.185, -0.190),
  lat  = 5.600
)
```

## Monitor readings from a CSV

Monitors have an identifier, a location, a date and a value. Daily, hourly or
monthly series are all fine.

```{r monitors}
set.seed(1)
days <- seq(as.Date("2018-01-01"), as.Date("2020-06-30"), by = "day")
monitors <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  data.frame(monitor = paste0("m", i),
             lon = c(-0.200, -0.186, -0.150)[i], lat = 5.6,
             date = days,
             pm25 = 40 + 10 * sin(2 * pi * as.numeric(days) / 365) + 5 * i +
               rnorm(length(days), sd = 4))
}))

src <- svy_exposure(monitors, unit = "monitor", value = "pm25")
src
```

Windows are offsets from each person's date, in days by default. Both ends
are included. Radii are in kilometres, and each combination of window and
radius is returned.

```{r assign}
res <- svy_expose(
  people, src,
  windows = list(prenatal = c(-270, -1), postnatal = c(0, 364),
                 cumulative = c(-270, 364)),
  radius_km = c(1, 5),
  name = "pm25"
)
res
```

`coverage` is the share of the window's days with a value. These monitors stop
at the end of June 2020, so the postnatal windows of the two latest births run
past the data. With the default `min_coverage = 0.75` their postnatal values
are `NA`, instead of a mean over only part of the year.

```{r coverage}
subset(res, window == "postnatal" & radius_km == "5",
       select = c(id, pm25, coverage, window_end))
```

## Choosing how monitors are combined

```{r assign-methods}
# A child 0.55 km from monitor m1 and 1 km from m2
child <- data.frame(id = 1, date = as.Date("2019-06-01"), lon = -0.195, lat = 5.6)
sapply(c("mean", "nearest", "idw"), function(a) {
  svy_expose(child, src, windows = list(w = c(-30, -1)),
             radius_km = 5, assign = a, name = "pm25")$pm25
})
```

## Calendar windows and interview dates

Windows can be given in weeks, months or years. If you have the interview date
and the child's age instead of the birth date, the anchor is derived for you.

```{r months}
survey <- transform(people, interview = date + 400, age_months = 13)
svy_expose(survey, src, date = "interview", date_is = "interview",
           age_months = "age_months",
           windows = list(prenatal = c(-9, 0)), window_unit = "months",
           radius_km = 5, name = "pm25")[, c("id", "pm25", "window_start", "window_end")]
```

## Rasters and area tables

The same call works for a raster stack with one layer per day, month or year,
a table of grid cells, or a table of district values. Only the first line
changes.

```{r other-sources, eval = FALSE}
src <- svy_exposure("pm25_monthly.tif")
src <- svy_exposure("cells.csv", type = "grid")
src <- svy_exposure("districts.csv", unit = "district",
                    boundaries = gadm2, boundary_id = "district")
```

Raster layers are dated from `terra::time()`, from dates in their names such as
`pm25_2019-03`, or from a `dates` argument. Layers longer than a day, such as
months, are weighted by the days that fall inside each window.

## Wide format for modelling

```{r wide}
svy_expose(people, src, windows = svy_windows("prenatal_postnatal"),
           radius_km = 5, name = "pm25", format = "wide")
```
